translated_project_reason_txt: Every year the natural forests in the uplands of the province where the water sources are born are reduced, which has caused the decline of the most important resource on the planet, water, year after year. We also ensure a supply of natural nutrients from these future forests and the capture of 3.5 metric tons per tree and per year of carbon dioxide when the trees are 20 years old.
translated_primary_goal_txt: reforestation of basins, sub-basins of the rivers that supply water to the province, reforestation of deforested areas, to guarantee in a certain way in the future the supply of water for human consumption and irrigation, and the capture of carbon dioxide to produce pure oxygen, this as a measure of adaptation and mitigation of climate change.

translated_project_description_txt: The Iron Sheets Loan Project is designed to support workers in improving their housing conditions by providing affordable loans to purchase iron sheets (roofing materials). Through this initiative workers will access quality roofing materials and repay the cost in manageable installments over an agreed period. The project aims to promote safe durable and decent housing while reducing the financial burden of making large upfront payments. It also contributes to workers’ welfare dignity and long-term socio-economic stability.
translated_project_reason_txt: Many workers live in inadequate housing due to low incomes making it difficult to afford durable roofing materials. As a result they face poor living conditions health risks and limited access to financing for home improvements compounded by low savings capacity.
translated_primary_goal_txt: Improved access to durable roofing will enhance workers’ living conditions dignity and overall well-being. It is expected to improve health outcomes boost morale and job satisfaction and reduce stress linked to poor housing. The loan scheme also promotes financial inclusion through affordable repayment plans while enabling long-term asset building for workers and their families ultimately contributing to higher productivity at work.

translated_project_description_txt: IEF is a project that provided solar loans to workers, but many workers are unable to repay these loans within a short period. We have therefore introduced a recovery project in which we pay the full loan amount at once, and the worker repays us back in manageable installments.
translated_project_reason_txt: The initial problem addressed by this project is that many borrowers are unable to repay their existing loans on time due to financial constraints, leading to accumulating debt and financial stress. To resolve this, the project proposes paying off the full loan amount on behalf of the borrowers, allowing them to repay in smaller, manageable installments
translated_primary_goal_txt: The expected results of the project include improved repayment rates, reduced financial pressure on borrowers, strengthened trust between lenders and borrowers, and enhanced financial stability for participants, ultimately creating a more sustainable loan recovery system.
subcategory: Climate Change Mitigation/Adaptation (Clean Energy, Agroforestry etc.)

translated_project_description_txt: This investment project aims to provide affordable loans to workers to enable them to purchase improved cooking stoves. The initiative seeks to improve workers’ living conditions while promoting sustainable energy use and reducing household expenses related to cooking fuel
translated_project_reason_txt: Before the implementation of this project many workers face several challenges including: High expenditure on cooking fuel such as firewood and charcoal Use of inefficient traditional stoves that consume more fuel Exposure to smoke leading to health issues such as respiratory problems Limited access to upfront capital to purchase improved stoves Environmental degradation due to excessive use of firewood
translated_primary_goal_txt: The implementation of this project is expected to bring multiple benefits including: Reduced household fuel costs due to energy-efficient stoves Improved health conditions as a result of reduced indoor air pollution Enhanced worker welfare and quality of life Increased productivity at work due to better health and reduced financial stress Contribution to environmental conservation through reduced deforestation Promotion of sustainable and clean energy practices within the community
subcategory: Climate Change Mitigation/Adaptation (Clean Energy, Agroforestry etc.)

translated_project_description_txt: This project focuses on improving the productivity and sustainability of tea plantations through proper field maintenance practices and the application of organic manure. The investment includes activities such as plucking weeding soil conservation and the use of organic fertilizers (such as buying animal manure) to restore soil fertility. The project aims to enhance tea quality and yield while reducing dependence on chemical fertilizers and promoting environmentally friendly farming practices
translated_project_reason_txt: The key challenges include declining soil fertility from continuous tea cultivation leading to reduced yields and lower green leaf quality. Farmers also face high fertilizer costs and limited access to inputs along with poor plantation management practices such as delayed pruning and inadequate weeding. In addition soil erosion limited knowledge of organic manure use and climate variability further negatively affect tea productivity.
translated_primary_goal_txt: The project is expected to increase tea production and improve leaf quality while restoring soil fertility and ensuring the long-term sustainability of plantations. It will reduce production costs by lowering dependence on chemical fertilizers and promote better environmental conservation and soil protection. Overall it will enhance farmers’ incomes improve knowledge and adoption of sustainable farming practices and strengthen the resilience of tea plantations to climate change.

Through environmental programs, currently, fishermen have increased their knowledge on the coastal ecosystems that they live in. translated_project_name: Delivery of wastewater systems, management of coffee honey water and personal protection elements, protection of coffee ecosystems.
translated_project_description_txt: Reduce the level of pollution generated by gray water and honey waters, in addition to reducing risks due to the inadequate management of pesticides and contributing to the conservation and protection of the environment
translated_project_reason_txt: Currently, having the diagnosis of beneficial infrastructure, additional points related to the management of honey and gray water have been identified, where it is observed that some of the septic systems are already in poor condition. With regard to the management of honey water, it has become evident that some farms do not have systems for the management of honey water, since most of them collect it for banana fertilization or irrigation through ditches in the crop lot. On the other hand, deterioration has been identified in the personal protection elements used by associates and their workers who carry out the activity of handling, storing and applying pesticides. In addition, during internal or external audit visits, if environmental risks or needs are identified, activities will be carried out to help improve environmental practices.
translated_primary_goal_txt: Delivering septic systems or systems such as acidogenic hydrolytic reactors for honey water management will reduce contamination of soils or water sources, so CAFICAICEDONIA will provide support to its associates in reducing risks of contamination due to coffee by-products or household wastewater. Provide personal protection elements to associates and workers when handling, storing and applying pesticides in order to make them aware of safety and health in farm work, while improving environmental practices that lead to environmental protection and conservation.

translated_project_name: management of the solution of non-compliances during internal and external audits and sustainable management of the environmental needs of the productive unit
translated_project_description_txt: In search of continuous improvement in compliance with FLOCERT criteria and to improve the practices or management of environmental needs that arise in the productive units of CAFISEVILLA's associates. In order to meet the above, identical needs have been identified in systems such as septic tanks and acidogenic hydrolitic reactors to provide adequate management of this water. The beneficiaries of the FLO premium project are members of the Seville cacaficulturers' cooperative - CAFISEVILLA.

translated_project_description_txt: The Indonesia Bali Green Project focuses on environmental sustainability, education, and cultural development. Key components include: Recycling Initiative: Waste management and recycling programs in villages. WIFI in Schools: Internet access for primary schools to improve learning. Extracurricular Activities: Free karate and cultural dance classes to preserve traditions. Reforestation: Planting native species to restore ecosystems. Community Education: Training on recycling and waste management.
translated_project_reason_txt: The needs assessment identified environmental challenges, limited educational resources, and cultural preservation as priorities. This project addresses these by reducing pollution, improving waste management, providing internet access for students, and offering cultural programs. It promotes sustainability, equal learning opportunities, and community well-being, aligning with Fair Trade’s goals of social and environmental development. What needs is this project addressing (how will it help/what situation will it change): Reduces pollution and improves waste management. Enhances education through internet access and extracurricular activities. Preserves cultural heritage and promotes biodiversity. Strengthens community health and sustainability practices. The assessment highlighted the need for better waste management, educational support, and cultural engagement. This project directly addresses these needs through recycling programs, internet access, and cultural activities.
translated_primary_goal_txt: The project will reduce waste and pollution, improve educational outcomes, and preserve cultural traditions. Impact will be measured through: Number of villages and schools implementing recycling programs. WIFI installation and usage reports. Participation in extracurricular activities. Reforestation progress and survival rates of planted trees. Beneficiaries include students, teachers, and community members, primarily in rural Indonesian villages.

translated_project_description_txt: The Tutaekuri-Waimate Stream Restoration and Protection Project aims to restore and protect the Waimate Stream along Chesterhope Station, which was severely impacted by Cyclone Gabrielle. The project involves fencing off stream edges and planting native vegetation to exclude livestock, stabilize banks, improve water quality, and enhance biodiversity. Initial work has already seen 700 meters fenced and planted in July 2025. This is a collaboration between the Joan Fernie Charitable Trust (JFCT) and Fair Trade, with plans to extend restoration along the entire stream boundary. Completion will involve continued planting, fencing, and monitoring with support from trustees and local volunteers.
translated_project_reason_txt: Cyclone Gabrielle caused significant flooding and erosion, leaving the stream vulnerable and degraded. The needs assessment and local context highlight the urgent need for environmental restoration to prevent further damage, improve water quality, and protect biodiversity. This project aligns with Fair Trade standards by supporting environmental sustainability and community engagement, ensuring long-term resilience and ecological health.
translated_primary_goal_txt: The project will: Exclude livestock from the stream to prevent contamination. Stabilize stream banks and reduce erosion. Improve water quality and restore natural habitats. Promote biodiversity and resilience against future weather events. Impact will be measured by: Length of stream fenced and planted. Survival rates of native plants. Water quality improvements and biodiversity indicators. Beneficiaries include local communities, environmental stakeholders, and future generations who rely on a healthy ecosystem.

translated_project_description_txt: Started in 2021, the Indonesia Bali Green Project promotes sustainability, education, and cultural development in villages. Key initiatives include: Recycling Programs: Waste management systems active in five villages, with plans to expand to more communities and schools. Wi-Fi in Schools: Internet access for primary students to enhance learning and teamwork. Extracurricular Activities: Free karate and cultural dance classes to preserve traditions and ensure accessibility. Reforestation: Planting native species to restore ecosystems and biodiversity. Community Education: Training on recycling and proper waste management practices. Planning Steps: Partner with schools and village leaders, run workshops, engage volunteers for reforestation and cultural programs, and monitor progress through regular reports. This project combines environmental action with cultural and educational support, creating lasting benefits for communities and ecosystems.
translated_project_reason_txt: • Environmental Need: Reduces pollution and improves waste management through recycling education and practices. • Educational Need: Provides internet access and extracurricular activities, enhancing learning opportunities and cultural engagement. • Community Development: Promotes sustainability, cultural preservation, and health awareness, improving overall quality of life.
translated_primary_goal_txt: The project is expected to improve environmental sustainability, education, and cultural engagement in Indonesian communities. Through initiatives such as recycling programs, school internet access, extracurricular activities, and reforestation, it will create long-term benefits for both students and local residents. Progress will be measured by participation rates, connectivity improvements, and reforestation records.

translated_project_description_txt: This project restores two vital waterways in Hawke’s Bay. Chesterhope Station, damaged by Cyclone Gabrielle, requires urgent planting of native vegetation along Waimate Stream to stabilize soil, prevent erosion, improve water quality, and create wildlife habitats. The Karamu Stream initiative builds on previous community-led efforts to enhance biodiversity and waterway health. Expanding native planting strengthens ecosystems, supports sustainable land management, and promotes kaitiakitanga (guardianship) values. Environmental Benefits: Native plants filter runoff, reducing pollution. Stabilized banks prevent erosion and flooding. Restored habitats protect native birds and wildlife. Community involvement ensures long-term care.
translated_project_reason_txt: Cyclone Recovery: Repairing severe damage at Chesterhope Station. Pollution Reduction: Filtering runoff to improve water quality. Sedimentation Control: Stabilizing stream banks to prevent soil erosion. Community Engagement: Involving local residents and Māori iwi in conservation. Wildlife Protection: Creating sanctuaries for native birds and biodiversity.
translated_primary_goal_txt: The project aims to restore and protect waterways at Chesterhope Station and Karamu Stream through native planting and community involvement. It will stabilize stream banks, reduce erosion, improve water quality, and create habitats for wildlife while promoting kaitiakitanga values. Impact will be measured by the number of trees planted, improved water clarity, and community participation.

translated_project_name: ENVIRONMENT: INSTALLATION OF SOLAR PANELS AND ELECTRICAL APPLIANCES
translated_project_description_txt: The project is an initiative that stems from the need identified in the needs assessment carried out by our committee in 2025, the idea is to install solar panels for the generation of electrical energy in homes that are owned by workers, helping to avoid environmental wear and tear by generating clean and renewable energy and providing appliances such as pots, heaters, air fryers, induction stoves, and others to gradually migrate to electrical energy from solar panels and eliminate the use of gas or wood burning appliances, thereby reducing the carbon footprint generated by all workers' homes within the scope of the certificate. The project will be funded 100% with the premium received by our committee.
translated_project_reason_txt: The results of the needs assessment showed that our workers and their families cook using mainly LP gas and this represents an expense that seriously impacts their economy when, without warning, they run out of gas to continue cooking and have to buy it overnight. In addition, as a second source of energy for cooking, many families use firewood, which when burned pollutes the atmosphere and increases the risk of families suffering respiratory diseases when they inhale the smoke that is generated. That is why there is a need for workers' homes to migrate and start using clean and renewable energies that do not cause pollution, seeking to make homes self-sustainable first by generating their own electricity and then equipping them with devices that work based on this electricity to meet the most basic needs such as electricity, hot water, cooking, etc.
translated_primary_goal_txt: Install solar panels to generate electricity in workers' homes and provide them with stoves, ovens, electric heaters, etc. to make it a self-sustainable home. The beneficiaries will be the workers of Edulag and Pentágono Agrícola and their families, approximately 300 people between children and adults. The impact will be measured in updates to the needs assessment when the number of people who rely on gas and firewood in addition to paying for the electricity they consume is getting lower and lower. In addition, the Fair Trade Committee will carry out the following activities: President: to follow up on projects and organize the other members of the committee and assign specific tasks for the execution of the project. Treasurer: keep track of premium expenses in the project. Secretary: draw up minutes of each project follow-up meeting. Vocals: support the specific activities of the project that are assigned to them.

translated_project_description_txt: Waste Classification at Home" Project is an environmental initiative funded by the Fair Trade Premium, aiming to encourage workers to practice waste segregation at source, thereby contributing to environmental protection and promoting green and sustainable living habits. Accordingly, each worker will be provided with one waste bin with separate compartments for waste sorting, along with environmentally friendly biodegradable garbage bags. translated_project_reason_txt: To control uncontrollable hazardous situations in the farm using appropriate Personal Protective Equipment.
translated_primary_goal_txt: To provide Personal Protective Equipment (hard hat, Farm boots and Cloth gloves) to registered Fair Trade Premium Participants to control uncontrollable hazards in the farm.

translated_project_description_txt: Fertilizers improve the supply of nutrients in the soil, directly affecting plant growth. Soil amendments improve a soil's physical condition (e.g. soil structure, water infiltration), indirectly affecting plant growth and productivity. Moreover, fertility has an impact on activities with an economic impact and is therefore related to economic growth and the fight against poverty.
translated_project_reason_txt: The Premium participants cannot buy Agricultural salt as fertilizer of the coconut trees to improve or enhance soil fertility to increase farm production
translated_primary_goal_txt: 204 Fair Trade Premium Farmers are the beneficiaries of this project to to enhance the fertility of the soil thru application of Agricultural salt as fertilizer to coconut trees to increase productivity resulting to the increase of the income of Premium participants or the farmers.

translated_project_description_txt: When crops are harvested, the nutrients follow the crop. Important nutrients are therefore removed from the soil. Often the soil is not able to replenish all the nutrients by itself, that is where fertilizers are crucial in supplying the nutrients that are lacking. In turn, this maximizes crop yield and quality. Fertilizers are key to rejuvenating the soil by providing nutrients the plants need to grow healthily either organic or non organic fertilizers.
translated_project_reason_txt: Farmers income from the coconut is not enough to sustain the daily needs because of unproductive coconut tree due to poor fertilization of coconuts
translated_primary_goal_txt: To increase the income of the Premium participants or the farmers by using of fertilizers because it enhances crop productivity or increases the volume of coconuts.

translated_project_name: SAFE HANDLING AND STORAGE OF AGROCHEMICALS:
translated_project_description_txt: The organization continues to work to minimize risks in the management and application of agrochemicals and has therefore made efforts to make it easier for associates to purchase EPP and warehouses for their storage, at a low cost. The priority in the short term is to correct the aspects that are critical to protecting the lives of producers and then to address those other aspects that contribute to the implementation of more sustainable production systems such as soil management. All of the above framed in the premise of guiding the coffee grower in the implementation of Good Agricultural Practices in each of the stages of the coffee production process.
translated_project_reason_txt: In order to protect life and health and complement awareness and training in the safe handling of agrochemicals, the Cooperative provided 81 associates with the purchase of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) in 2022. During the year 2022, 186 EPPs were purchased, of which 81 were delivered, mostly to associates who joined that year and to the promoters for the Agrochemicals container collection days.
translated_primary_goal_txt: Make associates aware of the importance of using appropriate protective elements for the application of agrochemicals and their proper storage. The equipment must consist of a complete anti-fluid dress, diving suit, nitrile gloves, mono goggles and a respirator with a filter suitable for the application of chemical products.

translated_project_description_txt: This program seeks the production of environmentally sustainable coffee by certifying farms. The sustainability of coffee farming is promoted through the adoption of good agricultural practices, a series of tasks that are carried out on farms for the care of nature, conservation of biodiversity and preservation of human health. For this purpose, training is provided to producers where they are made aware of the importance of BPA and the benefits they bring to their environment.
translated_project_reason_txt: Coffee production and the management of productive units are causing negative impacts to the environment that cause damage to biodiversity, the ecosystem and human health. This is mainly due to the lack of interest of producers in nature conservation and to the lack of knowledge of actions for better management of productive units to minimize the problem. This situation occurs in 80% of our partners' farms.
translated_primary_goal_txt: The program was intended to encourage more environmentally friendly coffee cultivation, preserving biodiversity and seeking ecosystem well-being; this was possible thanks to the certification of some farms where good agricultural practices were implemented. This certification meant the producer an extra income from the sale of their coffee and the provision of elements for personal care while carrying out hazardous work on the farm.
